cards.title: Shopping is becoming a show
cards.notes: The next shopping surface won't be a store, a search box or a chatbot. It'll be entertainment, and the story is what moves someone from feeling to buying.
cards.label: thesis

cards.title: How shopping moved
cards.notes: Three eras. Each one moved where persuasion happens.
cards.label: era

cards.title: Place · ~2006
cards.notes: You went to the store, physical or a website. You arrived with intent, and the brand controlled the room.
cards.label: era

cards.title: Feed · ~2014–2024
cards.notes: The store came to you. Instagram, TikTok and creators turned shopping into something that happens while you're doing something else. Brands lost the room.
cards.label: era

cards.title: Ambient · next
cards.notes: Shopping dissolves into entertainment. You're watching, not searching, and the purchase is a moment inside the experience.
cards.label: era

cards.title: Entertainment is the interface
cards.notes: Our position: AI changes shopping, but the long-term surface isn't someone typing to a chatbot.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: Typing is friction
cards.notes: A chat box asks people to know what they want and put it into words. That's work, and work isn't fun. Instagram won because it asks nothing of you.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: Desire is discovered, not described
cards.notes: Most wanting starts when you see something, not when you can articulate it. Stories create the want; a prompt can only answer it.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: AI works backstage
cards.notes: Agents are the stagehands, not the host: sizing, personalisation, stock, checkout, sequencing the show. The audience never sees the rigging.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: Some love shopping. Some hate it.
cards.notes: Shopping has always been two different activities sharing one word.
cards.label: shopper

cards.title: Ritual shoppers
cards.notes: Browsing is the point. Imagining a version of yourself, discovery, pleasure. Story deepens what they already enjoy.
cards.label: shopper

cards.title: Errand shoppers
cards.notes: Find it, buy it, leave. They skip browsing, but they'll still watch something good.
cards.label: shopper

cards.title: Story reaches both
cards.notes: A show doesn't feel like shopping. That makes it the rare format that serves people who love shopping and people who avoid it.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: Every group owns a medium
cards.notes: Groups took over different media and made them their own.
cards.label: audience

cards.title: Gen Z
cards.notes: Creator-native. TikTok as search engine. Trusts lo-fi and peer voices over polish.
cards.label: audience

cards.title: Millennials
cards.notes: Built the aspirational Instagram look and the DTC brand. Responds to identity and aesthetic.
cards.label: audience

cards.title: Gen X & Boomers
cards.notes: Email, YouTube long-form, search. Lower tolerance for novelty, high tolerance for depth.
cards.label: audience

cards.title: Geography rewrites the timeline
cards.notes: China's livestream commerce and super-apps (Douyin, Xiaohongshu) merged entertainment and checkout years ago. The West is catching up.
cards.label: audience

cards.title: Vertical is the shared grammar
cards.notes: Across every age and region, the phone held upright is the common frame. It's the one format everyone already speaks.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: The stage, not the feed
cards.notes: Our concept: a vertical story where the viewer's seat stays fixed and scenes are brought on and taken off.
cards.label: format

cards.title: Feed: camera over a bulletin board
cards.notes: The user roams a static page. Infinite, algorithmic, variable reward. It works like a slot machine.
cards.label: format

cards.title: Stage: the seat stays fixed
cards.notes: Content performs for the viewer. Authored, choreographed, composed at every scroll position.
cards.label: format

cards.title: Scroll is the projector crank
cards.notes: The viewer controls time, not space. Their input drives the show, so scrolling always does something.
cards.label: format

cards.title: A show that ends
cards.notes: Finite on purpose. An ending gives the story weight and gives the purchase a natural place to land.
cards.label: format

cards.title: From feeling to buying
cards.notes: Emotion is the engine; a physical product is the outcome.
cards.label: thesis

cards.title: Hook · Build · Proof · Close
cards.notes: Act structure doing the job a sales funnel used to do. The Story Builder's four beats.
cards.label: format

cards.title: Story makes the brand the search
cards.notes: "Find me running tights" is a spec fight. "Find me the tights from that run story" is already won.
cards.label: insight

cards.title: Value without purchase
cards.notes: Best-in-class brand stories are worth watching even if you never buy. If ours only works as a sales device, people will feel it.
cards.label: tension

cards.title: Where does the buy live?
cards.notes: Inside every scene, at an intermission, or at the curtain call? How do we sell without breaking the spell?
cards.label: question

cards.title: Questions for the room
cards.notes: What we want to pressure-test with creative leadership.
cards.label: question

cards.title: Luxury or friction?
cards.notes: In a world of infinite personalised feeds, is a finite, authored show a premium experience or an ask too far?
cards.label: question

cards.title: Episodes and seasons
cards.notes: Do stories become a series people return for, like a show, rather than one-off campaign pages?
cards.label: question

cards.title: Measuring emotion
cards.notes: Conversion is easy to count. How do we know a story landed: completion, replays, shares, return visits?
cards.label: question
